focus: RQ-6.1 to RQ-6.6: skill advisor alignment for a sibling ROUTER.md
answeredQuestions: RQ-6.1: What exactly does the freshness signature in runtime/lib/freshness.ts hash, and does a router move out of SKILL.md leave a stale checkout looking fresh?
RQ-6.2: How does runtime/scripts/skill_advisor_runtime.py discover and parse a skill, and what must change for it to read a sibling ROUTER.md?
RQ-6.3: What does the skill graph compiler in runtime/lib/skill-graph/ index and embed, and does it parse SKILL.md body text, Keywords comments or router markers?
RQ-6.4: What reads the leaf inventory, leaf-manifest.config.json and leaf-scopes, and does the router move change any of them?
RQ-6.5: Does any scorer lane read SKILL.md body text, keywords comments or router markers, and does the router move change scores or accuracy?
RQ-6.6: What do the advisor hooks, the plugin bridges and the routing-accuracy baseline scripts depend on, and what is the fix for each?
noveltyJustification: No prior lineage in this packet examined the advisor signature, watcher, projection or lane inputs, so all 21 findings are new to the packet.

label: The freshness signature probes only SKILL.md and graph-metadata.json per skill and folds both into one hash, so a ROUTER.md edit alone leaves the signature identical and deriveFreshness reports live against a graph that no longer matches the router.
The fingerprint loop skips a skill when SKILL.md is absent, so the fix must add ROUTER.md as a third signature probe while keeping the missing marker, not replace the SKILL.md probe.
The mtime fallback compares maxSourceMtimeMs against the SQLite artifact and a moved router adds no mtime to that maximum, so the fallback path carries the same blind spot as the signature path.

The OpenCode plugin bridge implements the same source signature a second time with its own delimiters and implementation paths, so a ROUTER.md probe must be added there too or plugin and daemon disagree about freshness.
The daemon watcher never sees a ROUTER.md write: it discovers skill-md, graph-metadata, derived key-file and optional doc-frontmatter targets but no router target.

Python discovery and parsing are router-blind by construction: discovery requires a SKILL.md join, and the frontmatter parser reads the header plus leading Keywords comments and returns at the first content line.
The Python record cache invalidates on the mtime and size of discovered SKILL.md files only, which is harmless while no router content is parsed and becomes a defect the moment the parser is widened.
The graph compiler reads only graph-metadata.json and never SKILL.md, so the compiled graph shape is unchanged and only the derived payload inside each metadata file could move.
Embeddings are description-only: skillDescriptionForEmbedding reads frontmatter description and feeds the skill_nodes embedding column at both write sites, so vectors do not move.
The doc-frontmatter harvest walks only references and assets and is gated off by default, so it cannot pick up a root ROUTER.md.

The leaf inventory is root-scoped, so a sibling ROUTER.md is not a leaf and leaf-manifest.json and leaf-aliases.json stay byte-stable, while the config note that describes the router as in-SKILL.md goes stale.

ROUTER.md is a governed root file that is required for the hub class and not forbidden for the standalone class, but the root-router check runs inside a hub guard, so a standalone skill carrying a ROUTER.md gets no validation.

No advisor code parses the MACHINE ROUTER section: package-wide searches for the section phrase and for the router.md filename match only the section heading, its pointer sentence, and the doc-file demotion rules.

No live scorer lane reads SKILL.md body text: the five lanes score intentSignals and keywords, name and description, BM25 field weights, derived triggers and keywords, and description, at weights 0.42, 0.28, 0.13, 0.12 and 0.05.
The explicit lane already treats router.md as a doc filename in both the suffix guard and the write-verb doc list, and the Python scorer mirrors it, so the new filename needs no lane change.

The accuracy hazard is an alias rather than a file read: the smart router phrase is hard-mapped to sk-code at 0.65 in the explicit lane, so a migration-shaped prompt can be captured before advisor vocabulary is consulted.

Derived extraction reads the whole body including code blocks and seeds sourceDocs, keyFiles and the provenance dependencies with SKILL.md, but its writer is deprecated and the fleet producer preserves curated fields, so committed derived does not move unless the deprecated extractor is re-run.
Hooks carry freshness and not content: the Claude hook and the CLI-fallback helper branch on the advisor envelope freshness, and the Pi extension is a symlink to the hook file inside the skill.

The three quoted accuracy numbers form a hash-pinned reproducible baseline: 155/195 at 0.7949, 49/66 at 0.7424 and 19/24 at 0.7917 with tau 0.03, captured with an empty database directory and filesystem projection.
The corpus driver runs the Python scorer as a subprocess, so a discovery or frontmatter change moves the baseline while a pure ROUTER.md move does not.

The stage-two replay that already reads a root ROUTER.md enumerates hubs only, so a standalone skill relocated router would be replayed by nothing, and the root-router contract header reserves the file for parent hubs.

direction: Treating the graph compiler as a SKILL.md body reader
reason: It reads only graph-metadata.json; it has no SKILL.md read at all.

direction: Adding a scorer lane for router markers
reason: No lane field exists for router content, and no lane reads body text.

direction: Adding ROUTER.md to the doc-frontmatter harvest
reason: The harvest walks references and assets only and is off by default.
